name: Dark Plum
lede: Dark Plum is a very deep, reddish purple that is nearly black, named after the skin of the ripe fruit.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Dark Plum is a descriptive name: the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files this swatch in a block of its own, and the xkcd survey of 2010 gave it the same words [1]. Its nearest named neighbor is [[aubergine]], about 2.9 units away on the CIEDE2000 scale, and the same ISCC-NBS system lists Port as a name for a related dark red-purple [1]. See also [[plum]] for the lighter fruit color.

One book use is worth keeping. Balfour-Paul quotes a traveller in southern Arabia who found that skin stained by indigo, sun and oil took on a bloom neither brown nor blue, something like a dark plum [2]. It is a reminder that indigo, usually thought of as blue, can go very dark and purple on the body [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This is a very rare color in painting. Only 1 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive has it covering at least 1 per cent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That says more about this archive than about painting: this swatch is almost [[black]], with a lightness of about 11 out of 100 [1].
